source.spoken_script: Someone took the body. That was Mary's first thought at the empty tomb of Jesus. The first day of the week, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene found the stone rolled away — and ran to Peter and John: They have taken away the Lord out of the sepulchre, and we know not where they have laid him. They ran. The body was gone. Only the linen — and the cloth that had covered his head: And the napkin, that was about his head, not lying with the linen clothes, but wrapped together in a place by itself. What thief wraps the face-cloth and lays it aside? Then John stepped inside. No angel. No risen Lord. Only the linen, lying where the body should have been. The gospel says only this: and he saw, and believed. Believed what? That his Lord was risen. He did not yet know the scripture — that Christ must rise from the dead. The linen was enough. Thomas refused to believe until he saw. Eight days later the risen Jesus showed him his hands — Thomas saw, and believed. Then Jesus said: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed. You were not at the tomb. You never saw the linen. Jesus was speaking about you. Believe what John believed at the linen — the Lord is risen. Already, he calls that faith blessed.

redteam:
VERDICT: REVISE

- youtube_short TITLE "What Thief Folds the Face-Cloth?" — the KJV says "wrapped together" (John 20:7) and the video's own narration says "What thief WRAPS the face-cloth". "Folds" is not the text's verb, and it deliberately echoes the debunked internet legend that a "folded napkin" was a Jewish dinner-table signal meaning "the master is coming back". This channel's whole premise is text-accuracy; do not import the legend's vocabulary into the title. FIX: "What Thief Wraps the Face-Cloth? The Empty Tomb".
- tiktok description, same offense: "What thief folds the face-cloth?" -> "What thief wraps the face-cloth?".
- youtube_short tag "folded napkin" and youtube_long tag "folded napkin meaning" — these SEO-target the legend and will pull viewers expecting the master-returns myth the video never teaches (off-thread promise). FIX: replace with "napkin wrapped together" / "john 20 7 napkin".
- facebook TITLE "No Angel. No Risen Lord. Only the Linen." — as a standalone headline this reads as a flat claim that there was no angel at the tomb, which contradicts Matthew 28:2-5, Luke 24:4, and John 20:12 itself (Mary sees two angels moments later). In the video the line is scoped to what Peter and John saw when THEY entered (John 20:1-10); the title strips that scope and a careful believer will call it misleading. FIX: scope it to John: "John Saw No Angel - Only the Linen. And He Believed."
- youtube_long description quotes John 20:2 ("They have taken away the Lord...") verbatim but unmarked, while John 20:29 gets quotation marks + (KJV). Inconsistent sourcing invites a "misquote" accusation even though the wording is exact. FIX: keep the wording, add the reference: '..."They have taken away the Lord out of the sepulchre, and we know not where they have laid him" (John 20:2, KJV).'
- John 20:29 quote itself checked word-for-word against KJV: VERBATIM. PASS on that line everywhere it appears.
- Titles otherwise honest, hook-true, no gain/loss or fear framing; platform tone and budgets fit; hashtags clean.
